varoulko-seaside.name: Varoulko Seaside
varoulko-seaside.why: Lefteris Lazarou (b. 1952) is a ship-cook's son who first cooked at sea at fifteen. He opened Varoulko in October 1987, and in 2002 became the first Greek chef ever awarded a Michelin star — the first the guide had given to Greek cuisine. In 2013 he moved the 'Seaside' room down to the Mikrolimano boardwalk, planting fine Greek seafood on the very quay the photo-menu touts work. When the guide relaunched a dedicated Greece edition in 2023 it did not restore the star: Varoulko now sits among the Selected, a loss the Athens food press noted pointedly.
varoulko-seaside.verdict: The most ambitious cooking of the Greek sea in Piraeus — restrained, precise, modern Aegean plating on the Mikrolimano water, a genuine fine-dining room dropped among the fish tavernas.
varoulko-seaside.signature: Grilled cuttlefish, caramelised lentils, orange: bittersweet, tender, precise.
varoulko-seaside.caveat: Not a taverna and not for a spontaneous cheap lunch — book ahead and expect fine-dining prices.
varoulko-seaside.person: Lefteris Lazarou (b. 1952), son of a ship's cook, went to sea to cook at 15; opened Varoulko in October 1987 and in 2002 became the first Greek chef ever awarded a Michelin star. Moved 'Seaside' to Mikrolimano in 2013.

dourabeis.name: Dourabeis
dourabeis.why: Giorgos Dourabeis, from Ios, and his wife Rallia, from Kythira, opened this fish house in 1932; three generations on, the porthole windows and 1950s Faliro photographs still watch the harbour, and the family — Sergios, Kostas and Rallis — still runs it. This is where a Piraiot brings a guest they want to impress, the counterpoint to every photo-menu terrace two coves over. In 2023 that plain-grill gospel reached the top of world dining when the two-Michelin-star Brazilian chef Alex Atala, of D.O.M. in São Paulo, chose it for an Athens meal and posted it.
dourabeis.verdict: Piraeus's benchmark old-guard fish house since 1932 — impeccable raw shellfish and salt-grilling at their most exacting, the standard every other harbour table is judged against.
dourabeis.signature: Marinated crawfish, silky-sweet in oil and lemon; then a whole fish salt-grilled over coals.
dourabeis.caveat: Not for a cheap taverna night — refined, dressed-up and priced like the institution it is; by-the-kilo bills climb fast.
dourabeis.person: Founded 1932 by Giorgos Dourabeis (from Ios) and Rallia (from Kythira), whose island roots still flavour the menu; run by the third generation — Sergios, Kostas and Rallis — today.

papaioannou.name: Papaioannou
papaioannou.why: Giorgos Papaioannou learned sea-cookery from his father in an early-1990s back-street fish shop, insisting the sea's gifts needed almost nothing done to them. He kept that when the flagship moved to the prime Mikrolimano waterfront in spring 2013 — on a horseshoe of touts, the one terrace that lets the fish speak. He still walks the market at dawn to choose the catch. The room now sits inside the Okyalos group, with a Mykonos outpost, and carries Athinorama's Greek Cuisine Award.
papaioannou.verdict: The one Mikrolimano waterfront table worth the splurge — minimalist, ultra-fresh catch cooked with restraint and respect.
papaioannou.signature: Catch-of-the-day whole fish, charcoal-grilled, dressed in ladolemono, filleted tableside — spotless.
papaioannou.caveat: Not cheap and not casual — fish is by the kilo and the bill climbs; not the place for a quick bite.
papaioannou.person: Giorgos Papaioannou — learned sea-cuisine from his father in an early-1990s back-street fish shop; still sources the daily catch at the market himself. Moved the flagship to the prime waterfront in spring 2013 (now part of the Okyalos group, with a Mykonos outpost).

margaro.name: Margaro
margaro.neighborhood: Hatzikyriakio · beside the Hellenic Naval Academy
tags: No bookings — put your name down
margaro.why: There is no card, and never has been: a grandchild wipes their hands and recites the four or five things the boats brought that morning, and if the shrimp are gone, they are gone. Margaró came off Ano Mera, Mykonos, in 1944; her son Lazaros took over in 1974 and pared the list down to fried fish, a Greek salad and the family's own retsina, pressed from vines in Markopoulo. Her grandchildren do the frying now, to her exact touch — three generations on the same corner, in the shadow of the Naval Academy.
margaro.address: Leof. Chatzikyriakou 126 & Ath. Miaouli, Hatzikyriakio, 185 39 Piraeus
margaro.verdict: The most honest fried-fish lunch in Piraeus — no menu and no bookings, just a short catch of whatever the boats landed and the family's own retsina, unchanged since 1944.
margaro.signature: Whole fried shrimp, shells lacquered and crackling, sweet flesh, lemon-squeezed, eaten shells and all.
margaro.caveat: Not for anyone wanting a menu, a booking, a sea view, or elbow room — it is benches, noise and a queue.
margaro.person: Founded 1944 by Margaró, a woman from Ano Mera, Mykonos; son Lazaros took over in 1974 and pared the list to fish, Greek salad and the family's retsina; her grandchildren do the frying now — three generations, same corner.

panorama.name: Panorama
panorama.why: Paraschos Manioudakis crossed from Crete to Piraeus to work the docks, and in 1957 he took a 1930s kafenio beside the chapel of Profitis Ilias and turned it into a taverna. It has climbed the Kastella hill with his family ever since; his grandson runs the pans now, three generations on the same terrace. The room has looked down on the port long enough to appear in the 1971 heist film The Burglars. From the tables the Acropolis stands off one shoulder and the Saronic opens off the other, Salamis and Aegina lying low on the water.
panorama.verdict: The fish is simply grilled and the portions run large, but at ~€38pp you pay for the highest sightline in Piraeus as much as the plate — worth the Kastella climb, not a fine-dining kitchen.
panorama.signature: Grilled fish of the day: whole, charred and glossy, dressed plainly, eaten over the whole Saronic Gulf.
panorama.caveat: Not for budget diners or anyone who won't climb Kastella — it's a hilltop, view-priced house.
panorama.person: Paraschos Manioudakis, a Cretan who came to Piraeus for the docks, opened it in 1957 on a 1930s kafenio site; his grandson runs it now — three generations.

oinomageireio-o-vasilis.name: Oinomageireio o Vasilis
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.neighborhood: Keratsini · inside the Ichthyoskala fish auction
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.why: The Keratsini ichthyoskala lands and auctions nearly all of Attica's fish before dawn. Vasilis and Valbona came from Albania some thirty years ago as newlyweds — she nineteen, he twenty-two; he worked a canteen seventeen years, she cleaned houses though she had studied classical music. In 2018 they took over an abandoned auction canteen, shut three or four years, and rebuilt it from tarps and pallets; their daughter Alexandra works the service. He crosses to the opposite dock at 3 a.m. to pick the day's fish and fries it a few metres from the tables. It is said to sustain eleven families.
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.hours: Daily lunch into afternoon; kitchen closes early — phone first
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.verdict: The realest place to eat fish in Piraeus — the auction's own catch fried a few metres from where the boats unload, eaten among the trawlers, forklifts and refrigerated trucks.
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.signature: Fried marides and a charred octopus tentacle, hauled from the auction dock hours earlier.
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.caveat: Not for refined decor, a wine list or a romantic evening — it is a canteen at a working fish market, lunch-first, closing early; hours can be irregular.
oinomageireio-o-vasilis.person: Vasilis and Valbona, who arrived from Albania ~30 years ago as newlyweds (she 19, he 22); he worked a canteen 17 years, she cleaned homes though she had studied classical music. In 2018 they took over an abandoned auction canteen and rebuilt it from tarps and pallets; daughter Alexandra helps in service.

to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.name: To Limanaki tou Giorgou
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.why: Chrysa and Giorgos have run this ouzeri for over thirty years on the little harbour of Keratsini, in the shadow of the shut-down DEH power station — its dead chimney and the COSCO cranes standing over the water. The arrangement that feeds the kitchen is old and simple: the harbour's fishermen eat half of what they land and sell Giorgos the rest, so the fish on your plate was on a caïque that morning. The couple read the day's freshness for you and steer you toward it without a sales pitch — a thing the laminated terraces two coves east cannot do.
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.address: Peloponisou & Propontidos (next to the ex-DEH power station), Keratsini 187 55
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.hours: Lunch and evening; weekends fill up — call ahead
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.verdict: One of the few ouzeris in Attica where the backdrop is a dead power station and the fish still costs €–€€ — a genuine neighbourhood favourite, not somewhere you go for the view.
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.signature: Fried barbounia and mussel saganaki: red mullet whole and sweet, mussels bubbling in spiced tomato, under an industrial skyline.
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.caveat: Not for anyone chasing a pretty seaside view — the backdrop is heavy industry and cranes, and weekends can mean a wait for a table.
to-limanaki-tou-giorgou.person: Chrysa and Giorgos, a husband-and-wife team who have run the harbour ouzeri for over thirty years, steering diners by the day's catch.

to-yperokeaneion.name: To Yperokeaneion
to-yperokeaneion.why: Andreas Kontsos captained ships out of Kimolos before he ever ran a kitchen, and he collected the relics of the sea — anchors, ropes, liner memorabilia. In the 1990s he made a Piraeus landmark called Karpouzi; a decade later he opened this eight-table room in a former nautical warehouse and named it Yperokeaneion, 'the ocean liner', after the great ships that once carried Greek migrants to Australia. His collection lines the walls, so dinner doubles as a small maritime museum, tucked above the Port Authority behind the old Chatzikyriakeio orphanage on the coast road.
to-yperokeaneion.hours: Dinner; ~8 tables plus a heated terrace — call ahead
to-yperokeaneion.verdict: A pocket seafood ouzeri of eight tables that pulls Italians and Athenians down to Hatzikyriakio at ~€20pp — worth the reservation for the room and the fish, not for anyone in a group or after meat.
to-yperokeaneion.signature: Charcoal-grilled sardines on oiled bread: charred, salt-bright, oily; and, on lucky nights, the owner's Kimolos ladenia.
to-yperokeaneion.caveat: Tiny and fish-only — not for large groups, walk-ins, or meat-eaters.
to-yperokeaneion.person: Andreas Kontsos, a ship's captain from Kimolos and collector of maritime antiques, who ran the 1990s landmark 'Karpouzi' before opening this room.

dyosmos.name: Dyosmos
dyosmos.why: The room is a neoclassical of 1920, drawn by the architect who owned it when he stepped off a boat from Constantinople and settled in Freattyda; the émigré's house now plates émigré recipes from the length of Greece. In the kitchen is Nikos Omaris, trained at Selini on Santorini, who assembles the menu ingredient by ingredient — Cretan staka, island fava, Xanthi kasseri, Eurytania prosciutto — each carried from a small named producer rather than a supplier. Stelios Parashos keeps the front. It has poured tsipouro to that formula since September 2015.
dyosmos.hours: Evenings and weekend lunch; call ahead
dyosmos.verdict: A meze kitchen built producer by producer, plating Cretan staka pasta and Schinousa fava in a 1920 neoclassical room with most small plates under €15 — the most identity-driven table in Freattyda, and not a sea-view fry-joint.

dyosmos.caveat: Not a sea-view harbour taverna nor a cheap-fry joint — it's an ingredient-led room.

ikariotiko-kafeneio.name: Ikariotiko Kafeneio
ikariotiko-kafeneio.neighborhood: Central Piraeus · Aristeidou St, off the port gates
ikariotiko-kafeneio.why: The kafenio has poured for the Ikarian diaspora for some seventy years, its walls hung with photographs and murals of the island the men left — sailors and shipyard hands trading stories of the sea over cheeses and olives brought from Ikaria itself. Nikos, thirty-five years behind the counter, is 'the Ikarian'. When the landlord took back the old room on Poseidonos in early 2023 — a 1956 building bound to become a hotel — the regulars simply carried the whole kafenio a few streets over to Aristeidou and set it down again, a floating piece of the island that refuses to sink.

ikariotiko-kafeneio.caveat: Not a destination dinner and no view — a smoky, no-frills community kafenio.

to-eidikon.name: To Eidikon
to-eidikon.neighborhood: Agios Dionysios · Psaron & Salaminos, behind the Papastrateio
tags: Weekday early evening, before the room fills
to-eidikon.why: Aristeidis Papakonstantinou came down from Gardiki, in Trikala, and opened this oinopantopoleio in 1920; his grandson, another Aristeidis, still draws the retsina from barrels in the cellar directly under the floor. Behind the hand-painted 'Εδώδιμα / Αποικιακά / Ρετσίνα Μεσογείων' shopfront sit a 1938 wooden ice-box, wind-up gramophones and Karagiozis figures. During the Occupation that barrel cellar became the quarter's air-raid shelter — people slept among the wine, and the bullets still mark the shutters. Voula cooks the five or six mezedes; the Papakonstantinou family are among the last in Greece pressing their own taverna wine.

to-eidikon.verdict: The last true barrel-wine oinopantopoleio in Piraeus — a 1920 room where the retsina is still pressed in the cellar directly below your table.
to-eidikon.signature: Cellar retsina: cold and resin-sharp, poured beside fried potatoes under four runny eggs.
to-eidikon.caveat: Not for anyone wanting a menu, a wine list or polish — five or six mezedes and barrel retsina, cash-simple, in a cramped old room.
to-eidikon.person: Family Papakonstantinou — founded 1920 by Aristeidis (from Gardiki, Trikala); now third generation, son Apostolos and grandson Aristeidis, with Voula cooking the mezedes.

propolemikon.name: Propolemikon
propolemikon.neighborhood: Agios Dionysios · Dervenakion St, behind the port
propolemikon.why: Perama shipwrights built this stone wine-house; it first poured as an oinomageireio in 1896, which makes it one of the oldest tavernas in Piraeus. In the pre-war years the room was a hearth of rebetiko — Markos Vamvakaris, Stratos Pagioumtzis, Anestis Delias and Giorgos Batis, the 'tetras' of Piraeus, played between these walls, and many well-known songs were written and sung here. The cellar barrels still hold wine made on site, and the kitchen still sends out the day's magirefta in the same Agios Dionysios back-streets. Live rebetika Saturday from 22:00, Sunday from 14:00.
propolemikon.hours: Evenings; rebetika Sat 22:00 & Sun 14:00 — call ahead
propolemikon.verdict: A stone-walled 1896 oinomageireio where the legendary Piraeus rembetiko quartet once played and the house wine still comes from cellar barrels.
propolemikon.signature: Barrel wine: rough, cold from the stone cellar, poured under walls that heard Vamvakaris play.
propolemikon.caveat: Not for a quiet, refined dinner — a smoky, music-first old room; phone to confirm it is open and whether there is rembetika that night.
propolemikon.person: Built by Perama karavomarangoi (shipwrights) as a wine house said to date to 1896 — among the oldest tavernas in Piraeus; the stone-cellar barrels still hold wine made on site.

to-koutouki-tou-antoni.name: To Koutouki tou Antoni
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.neighborhood: Palaia Kokkinia · alley above Thivon St
tags: A warm summer night in the courtyard
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.why: It has cooked continuously since 1958, in a lane above Thivon in Palaia Kokkinia — the quarter the 1922 refugees built. The covered courtyard is organised around a tall old fig tree with a whitewashed trunk; old tiles, embroidered cloths and real antiques make the room read like the parlour of an old refugee-quarter house. Athinorama called it a place where 'the old taverna lives in the neighbourhoods of Piraeus.' It keeps the name of its original Antonis; Eirini Vergopoulou holds it now, per the registry. Barrel wine comes by the karafa, and the joy is the yard, not the plating.
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.verdict: A 1958 Kokkinia koutouki built around a whitewashed fig tree, where floral-cloth tables and barrel wine make dinner feel like a refugee-quarter courtyard from another century.
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.signature: Bakaliaros skordalia: fried cod with fierce garlic-potato purée, barrel wine, under the fig tree.
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.caveat: Not for the design-conscious or the hurried — deliberately old, tiled and floral; the joy is the courtyard, not the plating.
to-koutouki-tou-antoni.person: Running since 1958 in the heart of the 1922 refugee quarter; held today by Eirini Vergopoulou per the business registry, keeping the name of its original Antonis.
